title: Tucker: World War Is Coming Soon
summary: Tucker Carlson monologue: a bigger US defence budget means a world war is coming soon, so the US must ally with Russia; NATO is finished.

assertions.quote: So, I think it's fair to expect and all the signs suggest that we're going to have a big war soon.
that's the kind of budget that a country that anticipates a global or regional war has for its military.

verdicts.note: The administration's motives are not on record; large budgets also reflect deterrence and industrial policy.

SIPRI finds US military spending fell 7.5 percent in 2025 to $954 billion, mainly because supplemental aid to Ukraine stopped; its stated priorities are nuclear modernization and deterring China, not preparing for an expected major war.

assertions.quote: We've been at war for four years. All of us are pretending we're not. we are.
We cannot survive a global conflict if Russia and China are aligned against us.

verdicts.note: The US and its allies outweigh Russia and China in economic output and naval power; the claim is a sweeping assertion.

assertions.quote: the last administration intentionally drove Russia into an alliance with China, which they now have.

verdicts.note: They declared a no-limits partnership and exercise together, but have no mutual-defence treaty.

DoD 2025: despite deeper ties, Beijing and Moscow 'remain unwilling to establish a formal defense alliance with mutual security guarantees', still distrust each other, and China has withheld lethal aid for Russia's war.
EFIS calls China and Russia 'allies without a treaty' and judges a formal military alliance unlikely in the near future, though joint exercises and R&D cooperation continue.
US intelligence calls cooperation among China, Russia, Iran and North Korea limited and primarily bilateral, constrained by divergent interests, which is not an alliance.

assertions.quote: With the help of NATO, which by the way is now done, NATO is done.

verdicts.note: NATO still functions: all 32 members met at the 2026 summit and Article 5 stands, though US commitment has weakened.

The survey expects NATO to endure: respondents split 35/35 on its future influence, 44% expect it to change form by 2036, 61% expect the US to keep its central role, and 65-75% of Americans back the commitment.

assertions.quote: if you are wondering whether volatility is coming up, look at silver prices. Look at gold prices over the last year.

verdicts.note: Precious metals rose on central-bank buying, interest rates and currency worries; prices do not single out war.
